titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 17, part 2
part: Spell 17, part 2 — Min's plumes, the double nest and the gates (Plates 7–8)
about: The second part of Spell 17 goes on with the dead man's statements and their commentary: he is Min wearing two plumes, he drives out his wrongs, he is purified in the double nest of Herakleopolis, he passes the gates of Rosetau and of the supports of Shu, and he asks the gods in the presence for their arms. After each statement a question in red ("What, then, is it?") brings in a gloss, often with further glosses introduced by "another saying". On the papyrus it runs from Plate 7, line 30, to Plate 8, line 70, and it ends with the statement that Ani raised up the hair at the time of the storm, which the next part explains.

sentences.l: I · Min · in · coming-forth-his · (iw) · have-set-I · two-plumes-his · upon · head-my
sentences.i: I am Min in his coming forth; I have set his two plumes upon my head.
sentences.n: A new statement. mnw 'Min' is the emblem of Min on a standard (coded R22 over R12; the drawing is uncertain in the print) with a seated god, as in the address to the gods after Spell 125 (Budge: Àmsu). prw·f 'his coming forth' is the house pr with r as complement, the chick w, walking legs and plural strokes, and ·f with its horns printed as a small cross: the noun prw from pri 'go forth', a god's appearing in procession. The top sign is a long flat rectangle in the print, taken as the house. iw opens the clause and is not translated. rdi·n·i 'I have set' is the mouth r and the giving arm di, then water n and the seated man: the sḏm·n·f with ·i. Budge takes it as a passive, 'may be given to me'; read rdi n·i, 'were given to me', the signs allow that too. šwty·f 'his two plumes' is the feather šw (H6), t and two oblique strokes y, the dual ending, with a tall double plume (coded S9) as classifier, and ·f; Budge's numeral 31 is printed inside the word. m tp·i 'upon my head': the owl m, the head with its stroke and ·i. Min of Coptos wears a crown of two tall plumes: to put on his plumes is to take his form.

sentences.l: who · then · indeed · he
sentences.i: Who, then, is he?
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the question in red, as in part 1. The first four signs of tr (t, r, the reed and the stem M6) stand in Budge's square brackets and are restored; the man with hand to mouth after them is printed. pw 'who?', tr and rf 'then', sw 'he': the question that opens each gloss.

sentences.l: as-for · Min · Horus · it-is · who-protects · father-his
sentences.i: As for Min, he is Horus, who protects his father.
sentences.n: ir 'as for' puts Min first as the topic, and ḥr pw 'it is Horus' answers. nḏ-ḥr 'who protects' is the sign nḏ, a knobbed staff (coded Aa27, approximate), with the pot nw standing for its n and a low sign (U15) as classifier, then the face ḥr with its stroke; Budge's numeral 32 is printed before the face. nḏ ḥr, literally 'care for the face of', is 'protect, look after', and nḏ-ḥr itf·f 'who protects his father' is the participle (Budge: net'-ḥrà, 'the avenger of'). itf·f 'his father' is the reed, t and the viper f with its horns, a seated man (coded A1, as in part 1; the type draws it like the god's figure) and ·f. Min, the god of Coptos, was taken as a form of Horus, the son who stands up for his dead father Osiris.

sentences.l: as-for · having-come-forth-his · birth-his · it-is
sentences.i: As for his coming forth, it is his birth.
sentences.n: prw·n·f is written like prw·f in line 30, but with water n before ·f in place of the plural strokes: the n of the sḏm·n·f, the verb form used here as a noun after ir, 'his having come forth'; the chick w may write an ending of the form. Budge reads peru-nef, 'his appearance'. msw·f 'his birth' is the three skins ms (F31) with s as complement and the chick w, a seated child with hand to mouth (coded A17; uncertain in the print) as classifier, ·f, and after the suffix a seated man (coded A1; the type draws it like the god's figure): read as mswt 'birth' with its t not written. For a god, coming forth into the world is being born.

sentences.l: as-for · two-plumes-his · upon · head-his · the-going · of-Isis · and · Nephthys · placed-they · it(?) · upon-head-his
sentences.i: As for his two plumes upon his head, that is Isis and Nephthys going and setting themselves(?) upon his head.
sentences.n: šwty·f 'his two plumes' is written here with the chick w after the feather, its complement; Budge's numeral 33 is printed inside it. šmt 'the going' is the pool with walking legs through it (N40, the sign šm) with m as complement, t and walking legs: the infinitive of šm 'go', with Isis and Nephthys after it as its subject; no pw is written. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat ꜣs with t, the egg and a cobra as classifiers. ḥnꜥ 'and, together with'. nbt-ḥwt 'Nephthys' is the basket on the house (coded O9, approximate) with a cobra. Budge's three groups erṭā, en and sen are joined here as rdi·n·sn 'they placed': the mouth and the giving arm, the n of the sḏm·n·f, and ·sn (the bolt, water n and plural strokes). sw 'him, it' is the singular dependent pronoun; the sense asks for 'themselves', as Budge renders, and the translation marks the doubt. ḥr-tp·f 'upon his head' is the face ḥr with r, then t and a small coil (coded Z7), which are not read, the head with its stroke, and ·f (Budge: ḥert-f); his numeral 34 is printed after the face. The two mourning sisters of Osiris become the two plumes of the crown.

sentences.l: are-they · as · the-kites · gather-they(?) · over · the-ailment · of-head-his
sentences.i: They are there as the two kites, and they gather(?) over what ails his head.
sentences.n: wnn·sn 'they are' is the hare wn with water n twice (n as complement and the second n of wnn) and ·sn. ḏrtw 'the kites' is the bundle ḏr (M36) with r as complement, t and the chick w each written twice, and two birds with long necks (coded G38, approximate): the signs are doubled for the pair, Isis and Nephthys as the two kites (Budge: t'ertutu, 'protectresses'). The second t and w are classifiers of the pair, not sounds. sꜣk·sn is the folded cloth s, the reed, the basket k and the vulture ꜣ (a crested bird in the print), with ·sn: read sꜣk 'gather, draw together', with the reed not read (Budge: sàka-sen, 'they provide'); the reading is not sure. ḥr 'over' is the face with its stroke. mn is the gaming board mn with n, a small cross (coded Z9, printed above the bird) and the bird of bad things as classifiers: the noun 'ailment', from mn 'suffer', with tp·f 'his head' after it as a direct genitive. Kites crying over the dead are the image of the two sisters mourning Osiris.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-uraei · great · mighty · they-are · which-are-upon · the-head · of-father-their · Atum
sentences.i: Another saying: they are the two great and mighty uraei which are upon the head of their father Atum.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red (the small flat sign under the cobra is coded D46). ꜥrwt 'the uraei' is the arm ꜥ, r, w and t with two cobras as classifiers: iꜥrwt, the plural of iꜥrt 'uraeus', with its reed not written; the two cobras show the pair. wrt 'great' (the swallow wr with r and t) and ꜥꜣt 'great, mighty' (the column ꜥꜣ, laid flat in the print and coded O29, approximate, with ꜥ, t and the roll) agree with it in the feminine. A pw is 'they are A'. imyt 'which are upon' is the crossed planks im with m and t, the feminine of imy, its y not written. tp itf·sn 'the head of their father': tp with its stroke, itf with the seated man (A1) and ·sn. tm 'Atum' is t, the sledge and the owl with a god, as in part 1. Here the two sisters are the rearing cobras on the brow of the creator.

sentences.l: another · saying · (n) · two-eyes-his · they-are · two-plumes-his · upon · head-his
sentences.i: Another saying: his two plumes upon his head are his two eyes.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes the whole gloss in red. Water n after ky ḏd has no clear place and is not translated. irty·f 'his two eyes' is the eye ir written twice, the second for the dual, with ·f: the dual of irt 'eye'. A pw B is 'B, they are A'. šwty·f 'his two plumes' with the chick w, as in line 32, and m tp·f 'upon his head'. The eyes of the sky god are the sun and the moon, and here they are the two plumes of his crown.

sentences.l: is · the-Osiris · the-scribe · of-the-offerings · of-the-gods · all · Ani · in · vindication · in · land-his · has-come-he · into · city-his
sentences.i: The Osiris, the scribe of the offerings of all the gods, Ani, is vindicated in his land; he has come into his city.
sentences.n: A new statement, made of the dead man in the third person. wnn 'is' is the hare wn with n twice: the verb 'be' opens the sentence, the Osiris Ani is its subject and m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'in vindication' its predicate. wsir with the tall seat Q1 and the eye. sš ḥtp nṯrw nbw 'scribe of the offerings of all the gods': the palette, then ḥtp, the loaf on the mat (R4) with t and p as complements, nṯrw, the flag with a seated god and a stroke (a thin dashed line in the print) for the plural, and nbw, the basket with plural strokes. In ꜣny 'Ani' water n and the plural strokes stand in Budge's square brackets and are restored. m mꜣꜥ-ḫrw: the m is the later owl (Aa15), and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written short, the plinth mꜣꜥ and the oar ḫrw alone. tꜣ·f 'his land' is the strip of land with grains (N16) and ·f. ii·n·f 'he has come' is the reeds with legs ii (M18) with i and walking legs, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·f. niwt·f 'his city' is the town sign with t and a stroke. The dead man comes home to his city as a god to his own town.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; sw 'it' is the city.

sentences.l: the-horizon · it-is · of · father-his · Atum
sentences.i: It is the horizon of his father Atum.
sentences.n: ꜣḫt 'horizon' is the sun between two hills ꜣḫ with t and the house sign (an open-bottomed box in the print), as in part 1. nt 'of' is the feminine genitive, agreeing with ꜣḫt. itf·f as in line 32. tm 'Atum' is written here with the later owl m (Aa15). The horizon, where the sun rises, is the city of the sun god, and so the home of his son.

sentences.l: drive-out-I · wrongs-my · dispel-I · evils-my
sentences.i: I drive out my wrongs; I dispel my evils.
sentences.n: A new statement. dr·i 'I drive out' is the hand d (squared at its end in the print), the mouth r and a low sign with a curled end (coded U15), the classifier of force, with ·i: the sḏm·f of dr 'drive away' (Budge: ṭer-à, 'I have made an end'). iwt·i 'my wrongs' is a young recumbent animal over t (coded E9, the newborn bubalis iw, approximate), the chick w and the bird of bad things, with ·i; the w may write the plural and is not read. Budge reads āut-à, 'my failings'; the first sign is not sure. ḫsr·i 'I dispel' is the placenta ḫ, the bolt s and the mouth r with a swab crossed by a bar (coded V29, approximate) and the low sign U15 as classifiers, and ·i (Budge: χersek-à, 'I have removed'). ḏwt·i 'my evils' is the mountain ḏw with w, t, plural strokes and the bad bird: the plural of ḏwt 'evil'. A god drives out what is wrong in him before he takes his seat among the gods.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; Budge's line 40 begins after tr.

sentences.l: is-cut · the-navel-cord · it-is · of · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · before · the-gods · all
sentences.i: It is the cutting of the navel cord of the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice before all the gods.
sentences.n: šꜥd·tw is the pool š (hatched in the print), the arm ꜥ and the hand d, with a notched cone pointing down (coded M44, approximate) and a knife over the low sign (T30, approximate, and U15) as classifiers of cutting, then t and w: the verb šꜥd 'cut' with the passive tw, 'is cut', standing here as a noun before pw (Budge: sāṭ-tu, 'the cutting off'). ẖpꜣ 'the navel cord' is a long stalk ending in a hatched knob (coded F32, the belly ẖ, approximate), the stool p, a bird (G41) that is not read, the vulture ꜣ and a small curl (coded Z7, approximate; it may be the pustule Aa2, the classifier of things of the body). Budge reads χapaa, 'the corruptible matter'; ẖpꜣ fits the signs that can be identified, but the reading is not sure. n 'of'. wsir with the low seat (Q2, approximate) and the eye. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'true of voice' is written short. ḫr nṯrw nbw 'before all the gods': ḫr is the placenta and r, nṯrw three flags, nbw the basket with w and a stroke. The cutting of the cord marks a birth: the dead man is born again.

sentences.l: is-driven-away · evil · all · that-is-his
sentences.i: All the evil that is his is driven away.
sentences.n: sḥri·tw 'is driven away' is the folded cloth s, the face ḥr with r, the reed i, a man striking with a stick (A24) and walking legs, then t and w: the causative of ḥri 'be far', 'remove, drive away', with the passive tw (Budge: seḥerà-tu). ḏwt 'evil' as in line 39, here without a suffix. nb 'all' is the basket alone; the t that would agree with ḏwt is not written. iry·f 'that is his' is the reed, r and two strokes y, the nisba iry 'belonging to', with a seated figure holding a staff (coded A52, approximate; it may be A1), the roll and a stroke (a thin dashed line) as classifiers, and ·f: written as iry 'keeper' is in part 1. Budge renders 'which belong to him'.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red. pw is written with the coil w (Z7), and Budge's numeral 42 follows it.

sentences.l: purification · it-is · on · the-day · of · is-born-he
sentences.i: It is purification on the day he is born.
sentences.n: wꜥb 'purification' is the vase pouring water over a foot (coded D60; the print shows a vase over an upright foot), the sign wꜥb, with water as classifier: here a noun, 'purity, cleansing'. m hrw 'on the day' is the courtyard h, r and w with the sun and a stroke. ms·tw·f 'he is born' is the skins ms with s, the woman giving birth (B3), then t and the coil w, and ·f: the passive msi·tw·f after the genitive n, 'the day of his being born' (Budge: mes-tuf). A newborn child is washed, and so is the god born again.

sentences.l: pure-am-I · in · two-nests-my · great · mighty · which-is · in · Herakleopolis
sentences.i: I am pure in my great and mighty double nest which is in Herakleopolis,
sentences.n: wꜥb·i 'I am pure' is wꜥb with water, the chick w and ·i. The w is not read: it may be a writing of the stative ending ·kwi with its k left out, and Budge renders 'I am purified'. sšwy·i 'my two nests' is a nest with young birds (coded G48) written twice for the dual, then w and two strokes y, the dual ending, and ·i (Budge: seś-ui-à, 'my double nest'). ꜥꜣt 'great' (the column laid flat, approximate) and wrt 'great, mighty' (the swallow with r and t) are written in the feminine, though sš is masculine. nty 'which is' is n, t and two strokes (a speck after n in the print). nni-nsw 'Herakleopolis' as in part 1: the sedge first, t, n, a seated figure (coded A42, approximate), two waters n, two strokes and the town sign. A nest is where a young bird hatches: the dead man is purified like a newborn god.

sentences.l: on-day · that · of · the-offerings · of-the-common-folk · to · god · that · great · who-is · in-it
sentences.i: on that day of the offerings of the common folk to that great god who is in it.
sentences.n: hrw pwy 'on that day', as in part 1, with pwy written with two reeds. ꜥbt 'offerings' is an upright with a crossbar and a foot (coded U23, approximate) for ꜥb, t, a lattice frame (coded Aa30, approximate), t again, which is not read, and the roll: the word read ꜥbt in Spell 1. Budge reads ābetet, but the arm and the leg of his reading are not printed. rḫyt 'the common folk' is the lapwing (G24) with a seated man, a seated woman (coded B1) and a stroke as classifiers of people. n nṯr pwy ꜥꜣ 'to that great god'. nty im·s 'who is in it': the reed, the owl m and the bolt ·s; 'it' is Herakleopolis, a feminine word. On the feast the common folk brought their gifts to the god of the town.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red; 'it' is the double nest.

sentences.l: Millions · the-name · of · the-one · Great-Green · the-name · of · the-other
sentences.i: 'Millions' is the name of the one, 'Great Green' is the name of the other.
sentences.n: ḥḥ 'Millions' is the kneeling god with raised arms (C11), the number a million, with two strokes (the second a thin dashed line in the print). A noun set before rn n X names X: 'Millions is the name of the one'. rn 'name' is the mouth and water n with the man with hand to mouth; wꜥ 'the one' is the harpoon with a stroke and the arm ꜥ as complement. Budge's two groups uat' and urà are joined here as wꜣḏ-wr 'the Great Green': the papyrus stem wꜣḏ (M14), the swallow wr with r, a reed that is not read (Budge's numeral 46 is printed before it), and three water lines over a pool as classifiers. ky 'the other' is the basket k and two reeds. The two nests are named for endless time and for the great water.

sentences.l: a-lake · it-is · of · natron · and · a-lake · it-is · of · […]
sentences.i: It is a lake of natron and a lake of […].
sentences.n: š 'lake' is the pool š with a stroke and a small sign like a canal (coded N21, approximate, as in other parts). ḥsmn 'natron' is the wick ḥ, the folded cloth s and the gaming board mn with n, then a tall sign like a pestle in a mortar (coded U32, approximate) and three grains (N33) as classifiers of minerals. The last word is a ligature of the owl m and the arm ꜥ, the column ꜥꜣ (laid flat, approximate) with ꜥ and ꜣ as complements, t and the house sign: read mꜥꜣt, which is not Maat, written otherwise. The word is not otherwise known and is shown as […]; Budge reads Māāāat and renders it 'nitre'. His numeral 47 is printed before its last two signs. Natron, the salt of the desert lakes, cleansed the body and the mouth: the lakes are places of purification.

sentences.l: another · saying · who-traverses · Millions · the-name · of · the-one · Great-Green · the-name · of · the-other
sentences.i: Another saying: 'He who traverses Millions' is the name of the one, 'Great Green' is the name of the other.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. smw is the folded cloth s, a flat bird-like sign on legs that cannot be identified (coded G38, approximate) and is not read, the owl m, the chick w and walking legs: taken as sm 'go, make one's way', a participle with ḥḥ after it as its object, 'who traverses Millions' (Budge: semu, 'traverser of'). The reading is not sure. wꜣḏ-wr is joined from Budge's two groups, as in line 45.

sentences.l: another · saying · who-begets · Millions · the-name · of · the-one · Great-Green · the-name · of · the-other
sentences.i: Another saying: 'He who begets Millions' is the name of the one, 'Great Green' is the name of the other.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red. wtt 'who begets' is the chick w and t twice, with a low sign with down-turned ends (coded D53, the phallus, approximate) as classifier: the participle of wtt 'beget'. wꜣḏ-wr joined as before. ky 'the other' here has a seated man after it.

sentences.l: as-for · (now) · the-god · great · who-is · in-it · Ra · it-is · himself
sentences.i: As for the great god who is in it, it is Ra himself.
sentences.n: After ir 'as for' stands ẖrt, the sign ẖr (T28) with r and t, which Budge leaves without English; the same group follows ir in lines 52 and 56 and in in line 69. It is taken as a writing of the particle grt 'now, moreover', which often follows ir, and is not translated apart; the reading is not sure, since the sign is ẖr, not g. nṯr ꜥꜣ 'the great god'. nty im·s 'who is in it', with the feminine ·s, as in line 45. rꜥ pw ḏs·f 'it is Ra himself': ḏs·f is the cobra ḏ, with the bolt s and ·f stacked under its neck in the print. The god of the town and of its nests is the sun himself.

sentences.l: have-gone-I · on · the-road · know-I · the-head(?) · in · the-Lake-of-Maat
sentences.i: I have gone on the road; I know the head(?) in the Lake of Maat.
sentences.n: A new statement. šm·n·i 'I have gone' is the pool with legs šm, m and walking legs, then the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i. ḥr wꜣt 'on the road': the face with its stroke, then the road with shrubs (N31) with t and a stroke. rḫ·n·i is the mouth r, the placenta ḫ and the roll, with n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f of rḫ, 'I have learned', that is, 'I know'. tp is the head with its stroke and a thin dashed stroke; Budge renders 'the heads (?)', and the sense here is not sure. š-mꜣꜥt 'the Lake of Maat' is the pool š (printed with a row of dots inside) with a stroke and the canal sign (approximate), then the sickle mꜣ (approximate) laid over the arm ꜥ, the vulture ꜣ, t, two feathers (coded H6) and the town sign (Budge: Śe-Maāat). The road brings the dead man to the lake where he is washed.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red.

sentences.l: as-for · Rosetau · (pw) · the-gate · it-is · southern · of · Naref · the-gate · northern · of · the-Mound
sentences.i: As for Rosetau, it is the southern gate of Naref, the northern gate of the Mound.
sentences.n: rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'Rosetau' is the mouth rꜣ with a stroke, a coil on a stick (coded V2) for sṯꜣ, a stroke, plural strokes and the desert hills (coded N25, approximate), as in Spell 1. pw stands after the topic, as in ir nḥḥ pw in part 1, and again after the next noun. That noun, here and after rst n iꜣrrd-f, is the star N14 with ꜣ, w, t and the house sign (an open box, approximate). The star writes both sbꜣ 'gate' and dwꜣ in dwꜣt 'the Duat', and Budge reads the same signs ṭuaut, 'the underworld', the first time and sebaut, 'the door', the second; the pairing of south and north asks for the same word both times, read sbꜣwt 'gate'. The reading is not sure. rst 'southern' is the plant rs with t, the canal sign (approximate) and a stroke; mḥty 'northern' is the crown of the north mḥ with t and two strokes y. iꜣrrd-f 'Naref' is written without the n that the name has in the introduction to Spell 125: the vulture and the reed (in that order), r, a cord with tails (coded T12, approximate) for rd, an open box (approximate) and ·f with its horns, with the town sign (Budge: Naàrutf). iꜣt 'the Mound' is the reed, ꜣ and t with a dome inside a frame (coded O20, approximate), a stroke and the canal sign. Rosetau, the cemetery land of Memphis, is here the passage between two holy places of Osiris.

sentences.l: as-for · (now) · the-Lake-of-Maat · Abydos · it-is
sentences.i: As for the Lake of Maat, it is Abydos.
sentences.n: ir ẖrt as in line 49. š-mꜣꜥt as in line 50, again with dots inside the pool; Budge's numeral 53 is printed inside the word. ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is an upright staff with a crossbar and two oblique strokes, like the sign of life (coded S34, approximate), taken as the sign ꜣb, with b as complement, the mountain ḏw with w and the town sign (Budge: Àbṭu). Abydos, the town of Osiris, kept the lake of his mysteries.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-road · it-is · on-which-went · father-his · Atum · upon-it · when · set-out-he · to · the-Field-of-Reeds · that
sentences.i: Another saying: it is the road on which his father Atum went when he set out for that Field of Reeds
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red (the flat sign at the cobra's tail is coded D46; it is close to Y1). wꜣt pw 'it is the road'. Budge's groups śemt and en are joined here as šmt·n: šm with m, t and walking legs, then the n, the relative form of the sḏm·n·f, 'on which … went', with t for the feminine, agreeing with wꜣt; ḥr·s 'upon it' takes up the road. itf·f has a bearded god-like figure here (coded A40), and Budge's numeral 54 is printed inside the word. tm 'Atum' is t, the sledge and a god. ḫft 'when' with wḏꜣ·f 'he set out': the chick w and a tall tapering sign ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate), ꜣ, walking legs and ·f. sḫt-iꜣrw 'the Field of Reeds' is one word, as in Spell 72: the field sign sḫt with t (a small forked sign under it, approximate) and a stroke, then i, ꜣ, r and w with a plant classifier (approximate), plural strokes and the town sign. pw after it is the demonstrative 'that'.

sentences.l: which-brings-forth · the-food · of · the-gods · behind · the-shrine
sentences.i: which brings forth the food of the gods behind the shrine.
sentences.n: mst 'which brings forth' is the skins ms with s, t and a crouching figure over a small stand, read as the woman giving birth (B3, approximate): the participle of msi, feminine to agree with sḫt. ḏfꜣw 'food' is the cobra ḏ, the viper f with its horns, ꜣ and w, with two strokes, a duck-like bird with raised tail (coded G38, approximate), a flat bar with a bowl on it (coded R4, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers (Budge: t'efaui, 'the tchefa food'). n nṯrw 'of the gods', three flags with a god and a stroke. ḥꜣ 'behind' is the plant ḥꜣ with ꜣ and the back of a head as classifier (coded D1, approximate), as in Spell 22. kꜣri 'the shrine' is the arms kꜣ, r and the reed, with a shrine with a cornice (coded O18, approximate), a house sign and plural strokes (Budge: kerà). The Field of Reeds yields the gods' offerings.

sentences.l: as-for · (now) · the-gate · that · holy(?) · the-gate · it-is · of · the-supports · of-Shu
sentences.i: As for that holy(?) gate, it is the gate of the supports of Shu.
sentences.n: ir ẖrt as in line 49. sbꜣt 'gate' is the star with ꜣ, t and the house sign, and pw after it is the demonstrative 'that'. The next word is a low sign with an upturned end and a long arm rising at its right (coded U15, approximate), r, t and a flat bar with a bowl on it (coded R4, approximate), on which t sits. It is taken as the arm holding a flail, ḏsr 'holy', with r and t: ḏsrt, agreeing with sbꜣt. Budge reads sert and takes it as a name, Sert; the reading is not sure. sbꜣ pw 'it is the gate', the star with ꜣ and the house sign. sṯsw 'the supports' as in part 1: the bolt, the rope ṯ (approximate) and the bolt, a crooked post (coded O30, approximate; the forked post of part 1) and the sky with drooping ends (approximate) over two strokes. šw 'Shu' with the chick w and a god. Shu holds up the sky; his supports stand at the edge of the world.

sentences.l: as-for · the-gate · northern · of · the-Duat · it-is
sentences.i: It is the northern gate of the Duat.
sentences.n: Here ir sets the whole phrase first as the topic and pw closes it: 'as for the northern gate of the Duat, it is (this)', that is, the gate of the supports of Shu is the northern gate of the Duat. sbꜣ is the folded cloth s, the star, the foot b and ꜣ, with the house sign and a curved shaft with a barbed end (coded M3, approximate) as the classifier of wooden things; s, b and ꜣ are complements. mḥty 'northern' as in line 52. dwꜣt 'the Duat' is the star dwꜣ with ꜣ, t and the house sign, as in Spell 22.

sentences.l: another · saying · the-two-leaves · of-door · that · through-which-went · Atum · upon-it · when · set-out-he · (from) · the-horizon · eastern · of · the-sky
sentences.i: Another saying: they are the two leaves of that door through which Atum went when he set out from the eastern horizon of the sky.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ky ḏd in red (the flat sign under the cobra is coded D46; it is close to Y1). ꜥꜣwy 'the two door-leaves' is the column ꜥꜣ (laid flat over the arm, approximate) with ꜥ, w and two strokes y, the dual ending, and two door-leaves (O31) as classifiers. ry is the mouth r with two strokes and two reeds and a branch with a barbed end (coded M3, approximate) as the classifier of wood: taken as rꜣ 'door, opening' in a later spelling with no ꜣ written (Budge: rei, 'of door'); the reading is not sure. pwy 'that' is written with the coil w. Budge's groups ut'a and en are joined as wḏꜣ·n, the relative form of the sḏm·n·f, 'through which … went', as šmt·n in line 53; ḥr·f 'upon it' takes up the door. tmw 'Atum' is t, the sledge, the later owl m and w with a god. ꜣḫt iꜣbty nt pt 'the eastern horizon of the sky' as in part 1; no preposition is written before it, and 'from' is supplied from the sense, as Budge does. At sunrise the door of the eastern horizon opens for the sun to come out.

sentences.l: those-who-are-in · the-presence · give · to-me · two-arms-your
sentences.i: You who are in the presence, give me your two arms!
sentences.n: A new speech, to the gods. imyw-bꜣḥ 'those who are in the presence' is the crossed planks im with m, two strokes y and w, then the phallus bꜣḥ (D53) with a god and a stroke: the plural of imy with bꜣḥ 'presence', the gods who stand before the creator (Budge: àmiu-baḥ). No 'O' is written before them. Budge's group àmmā-nà is split here into two words: imi 'give!', the reed, the owl m and the later owl m with the arm as classifier, the imperative of rdi; and n·i 'to me', water n and the seated man. ꜥwy·tn 'your two arms' is the arm written twice, two strokes y and w, then ·tn: t, n and plural strokes; t stands in Budge's square brackets and is restored. To give the arms is to reach out and draw the newcomer in.

sentences.l: I · god · that · (n) · came-into-being-I · among-you
sentences.i: I am that god; I came into being among you.
sentences.n: ink nṯr pwy 'I am that god'. Water n at the start of line 60 has no clear place and is not translated. ḫpr·n·i 'I came into being' is the scarab with r, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i (Budge: χeper-nà, 'I shall come into existence'). im·tn 'among you' is the reed and the owl m with ·tn; again t stands in Budge's square brackets and is restored.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red.

sentences.l: the-blood · it-is · which-came-forth · from · the-phallus · of · Ra · after · set-out-he · to · doing · a-cutting · on-him · himself
sentences.i: It is the blood which came forth from the phallus of Ra after he set about cutting himself.
sentences.n: snf 'blood' is the bolt s, water n and the viper f (with its horns), with a dotted line rising in an arc (coded D26, approximate) as the classifier of blood, and a stroke. pr 'which came forth' is the house pr with r and walking legs, the participle of pri. ḥnnw 'the phallus' is written as in part 1 (the hoe U6 over two waters, approximate). m-ḫt 'after' is the owl m and a branch (M3, ḫt) with ḫ and t as complements and walking legs, as in Spell 1. wꜣ·f 'he set out' is the lasso wꜣ (V4) with ꜣ and the road as classifier, and ·f: wꜣ r with an infinitive is 'set out to, set about' (Budge: ua-f). irt 'doing' is the eye ir with t, the infinitive of iri. šꜥd 'a cutting' is the pool (drawn as a box with a double slash; approximate), the arm, a long flat sign coded D46 (it may be Y1), the spiky cone (approximate) and the knife, with plural strokes, written as šꜥd in line 40; Budge's numeral 62 is printed inside the word, and he reads śāt, 'the mutilation'. im·f ḏs·f 'on himself'. From the blood of the sun's own wound come the gods named in the next line.

sentences.l: then-they · came-into-being · as · the-gods · who-are-in · the-following · of-Ra · Hu · and · Sia
sentences.i: Then they came into being as the gods who are in the following of Ra, Hu and Sia.
sentences.n: ꜥḥꜥ·n is the mast ꜥḥꜥ with ꜥ as complement and water n: the auxiliary 'then', which opens a narrative sentence. The chick w and the stroke after it are taken as ·w 'they', the subject pronoun of later Egyptian (Budge: āḥā-nu, 'They'); the reading is not sure. ḫpr 'came into being' is the scarab with r. imyw-ḫt 'who are in the following of' is im with m, two strokes y and w, a god and a stroke, then the branch ḫt with ḫ, t and walking legs, as m-ḫt above; Budge's numeral 63 is printed before the branch. rꜥ 'Ra' with r, ꜥ and the god. ḥw 'Hu' is the wick ḥ and w, a thin bar with a bent end (coded Aa15, approximate) and a flat bar with a bowl (coded R4, approximate), not read, and a god. siꜣ 'Sia' is a slanting roll of cloth (coded S32, approximate), the sign siꜣ, with ꜣ and a god. Hu, the word that commands, and Sia, the mind that perceives, are the powers by which the creator made the world.

sentences.l: are-they · following · Atum · in · the-round · of-the-day · of · day · every
sentences.i: and they are in the following of Atum in the daily round, every day.
sentences.n: wnn·sn 'they are', as in line 34. m-ḫt 'following, behind' as in line 61, here with a person after it. tmw 'Atum' is written with w; Budge's numeral 64 is printed inside the word. mꜥ is the owl and the arm: the preposition m in the later spelling mꜥ. ẖrt hrw 'the daily round', literally 'what belongs to the day', is the sign ẖr with r, t and the roll, then hrw 'day'. nt rꜥ nb 'of every day': rꜥ, the sun with its stroke, is here 'day' (Budge reads hru), and nb 'every'. The gods of the creator's word and mind go with him on his course every day.

sentences.l: (iw) · have-filled-I · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · for-you · the-Wedjat · after · was-harmed(?)-it
sentences.i: I, the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, have filled the Wedjat for you after it was harmed(?),
sentences.n: A new statement; iw opens it. mḥ·n·i 'I have filled' is the crown of the north mḥ (V22), with a flat bar with a bowl on it (coded R4, approximate) as classifier, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i; the name and title after it stand beside ·i, 'I, the Osiris Ani'. ꜣny here ends with the seated man on a chair (A51). mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written with the sickle mꜣ before the plinth mꜣꜥ, the arm ꜥ and the oar. The papyrus writes n·k wḏꜣt in red: n with the basket ·k, 'for you', then wḏꜣt 'the Wedjat', the chick w, a tall tapering sign ḏꜣ (coded U28, approximate), ꜣ, t and the eye with the falcon's markings (D10). hꜣb·s is the courtyard h, ꜣ and the foot b with walking legs and the bird of bad things, and the bolt ·s, 'it', the Eye; Budge's numeral 66 is printed before the bird, he renders 'after it had failed', and he prints a plain h. A verb hꜣb with this sense is not otherwise known: the translation follows the classifier, and the reading is doubtful. To fill the Eye is to make it whole again, and every offering is an Eye of Horus restored.

sentences.l: on-day · that · of · the-fighting · of-the-Two-Companions
sentences.i: on that day of the fighting of the Two Companions.
sentences.n: ꜥḥꜣ 'fighting' is written as in part 1: the pair coded O26 + N29 (approximate) with ꜣ and the low sign U15; the reading follows Spell 1 and is not sure, and Budge reads āba. rḥwy 'the Two Companions' is the mouth r with a stroke, the wick ḥ and w, with two gods: the dual of rḥ 'companion', its ending y not written, Horus and Seth (Budge: Reḥu, 'the two Fighters'). In their fight Seth hurt the eye of Horus, and Thoth made it whole.

sentences.l: what · then · indeed · it
sentences.i: What, then, is it?
sentences.n: The question, in red.

sentences.l: the-day · it-is · of · the-fighting · of-Horus · on-it · with · Seth · in · casting · filth(?) · in · the-face · of-Horus · seizing · Horus · the-testicles · of · Seth
sentences.i: It is the day on which Horus fought with Seth, when Seth cast filth(?) in the face of Horus and Horus seized the testicles of Seth.
sentences.n: hrw pwy 'it is the day': pwy, with two reeds, here does the work of pw. ꜥḥꜣ as in line 66, with ḥr 'Horus' after it as its subject, im·f 'on it', the day, and ḥnꜥ stẖ 'with Seth'. stẖ 'Seth' is the bolt, t and a small hatched sign (coded N37, approximate), taken as the placenta ẖ, with a god (Budge: Set). m wd 'in casting' is the chick w and the hand d (a flat sign in the print; it may be Y1) with a small cross and the low sign U15 as classifiers: the infinitive of wdi 'put, cast', after m; Seth, named before, is taken as its subject. stw 'filth(?)' is the folded cloth s and t with a cup-like sign (coded W10, approximate), a spiral (coded Z7, approximate) for w, and walking legs: the word read stꜣt in part 1, here without ꜣ (Budge: setau, 'excrement'); the reading is doubtful. m ḥr ḥr 'in the face of Horus'. iṯt is the tether ṯ on walking legs (the sign iṯ, coded as V13 and D54), t and the low sign U15: the infinitive of iṯi 'seize', with ḥr 'Horus' as its subject (Budge: θet, 'carried off'). ẖrwy 'the testicles' is the sign ẖr with r, w and two strokes y, the dual ending, and a pouch-shaped classifier (coded F51, approximate); Budge's numeral 69 is printed before it. In the struggle for the throne of Osiris each god maimed the other.

sentences.l: (in) · (now) · Thoth · who-did · this · with · fingers-his · himself
sentences.i: And it was Thoth who did this with his own fingers.
sentences.n: in with a noun and a participle singles out the doer: in ḏḥwty ir nn 'it was Thoth who did this'. ẖrt after in is the group of line 49, taken as grt 'now, and'. ḏḥwty 'Thoth' is the ibis on a standard with t, two strokes and a god. ir 'who did' is the eye alone, the participle of iri. nn 'this' is two sedges and two waters n, as in part 1. ḏbꜥw·f 'his fingers' is the finger ḏbꜥ (D50) written three times for the plural, with ·f, and two strokes after the suffix (Budge: t'ebā-f). ḏs·f 'himself': with his own fingers. Thoth, the healer among the gods, made whole the wounds of both.

sentences.l: (m) · have-raised-I · the-hair · at · the-time · of · the-storm
sentences.i: I have raised up the hair at the time of the storm.
sentences.n: A new statement. The later owl m (Aa15) that opens it has no clear place and is not translated. sṯs·n·i 'I have raised up' is the bolt s, then, after Budge's numeral 70, a crooked post (coded O30, approximate), here carrying ṯs as the post of wṯs 'lift' does, and the low sign U15 as the classifier of force, with the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i: written without the rope ṯ that sṯs has in line 56 and in part 1. šn 'the hair' is the cord šn (V7) with n and a lock of hair (D3) with plural strokes (Budge: śen). m tr 'at the time' is t, r, the reed and the stem tr with the sun as classifier: tr 'season, time'. nšny 'the storm' is water n, the pool š (with a double slash in the print), n and two strokes y, with the U15 classifier of force and the sky with falling rain (N4): from nšn 'rage' (Budge: neśeni, 'storms in the sky'). The part ends here; the question 'What, then, is it?' and its gloss begin the next part.
